title: Douglas Fir: Giant Douglas Firs You Can Visit
meta_description: Portland's tallest tree is 74 metres. Brussels' tallest is 33, and it is the same species. Four Douglas firs mapped, on three continents.
intro: The tallest tree in Portland is 74 metres. The tallest tree in Brussels is 33, and it is the same species. That gap is not about care or soil, it is about home ground: Douglas fir grows wild down the Pacific coast, and the one in Portland's Balch Creek canyon is simply standing where it belongs. Everywhere else it is an import with a hard start date, since seed only left the Pacific Northwest for Europe in 1827. Caserta's register claims about two hundred years for its forty metre specimen, which would put it in the ground the year before that, so read the figure as a round number. Hobart's went into the botanical gardens in 1894, seven years before the Australian colonies became a country. Brussels' grew up beside a racecourse that had two grandstands by 1878.
